newsitem.title: USA: Emery plans $55.9 mln expansion in Dayton.
newsitem.headline: Emery plans $55.9 mln expansion in Dayton.

text.p: Emery Worldwide, which moves more than four million pounds of freight a day through the Dayton, Ohio airport, said Monday it plans a $55.9 million expansion of its center there.
The expansion will increase capacity by 33 percent. Construction will begin in the fall and is expected to be completed by 2000, a company spokesman said.
Built in 1981 to serve as Emery's centralized freight processing center for North American shipment distribution, the hub has tripled in size to a 590,000-square-foot-complex.
More than 2,000 employees work at the facility.

Emery Worldwide, a subsidiary of CNF Transportation Inc, has scheduled a news conference on July 15 at the Dayton airport to provide details of the five-phase expansion program, which will include a new package sorting system.
